facts.one_liner: The Green Bay Packers’ storied bowl, the NFL’s oldest continuously operating stadium.
facts.why_go: Opened in 1957, Lambeau Field is home to the community-owned Green Bay Packers and is the oldest continuously operating stadium in the NFL. Its brick-faced Atrium houses the Packers Hall of Fame, and stadium tours take you through the players’ tunnel. Game days bring legendary tailgating in the surrounding neighbourhood.
facts.best_time: September–January for the NFL season (frozen ‘Lambeau’ games in December are a rite of passage); tours run year-round.
facts.how_to_get_there: Green Bay Austin Straubel International Airport (GRB) is about 10 minutes away; Milwaukee is about two hours’ drive.
facts.good_to_know: Game tickets sell out far in advance; the Hall of Fame and tours are easier to book.

facts.one_liner: Palm trees and the San Gabriel Mountains frame the Dodgers’ mid-century ballpark in Chavez Ravine.
facts.why_go: Opened in 1962, Dodger Stadium is the third-oldest ballpark in Major League Baseball, after Fenway Park and Wrigley Field. Its wavy outfield pavilion roofs, hillside palms and sunset views across Elysian Park to the mountains make it one of the most beautiful places to watch a game, and it has hosted World Series, the 1984 Olympic baseball events and countless concerts.
facts.best_time: April–September for the regular season; summer evenings for sunset first pitches.
facts.how_to_get_there: In Chavez Ravine near Downtown LA; the free Dodger Stadium Express bus runs from Union Station on game days.
facts.good_to_know: Traffic is heavy—arrive early. Ballpark tours run on many non-game days.

facts.one_liner: A 1922 stadium set in the leafy Arroyo Seco beneath the San Gabriel Mountains.
facts.why_go: The Rose Bowl opened in 1922 and is a U.S. National Historic Landmark. It hosts the annual Rose Bowl college football game on New Year’s Day, and has staged the 1994 FIFA World Cup final, the 1999 Women’s World Cup final and Olympic football in 1932 and 1984. Around it, the Arroyo Seco loop is a favourite running and cycling route, and a huge flea market fills the grounds monthly.
facts.best_time: January 1 for the Rose Parade and Rose Bowl Game; the second Sunday of each month for the flea market.
facts.how_to_get_there: In Pasadena, about 20 minutes’ drive from Downtown Los Angeles; Metro A Line to Memorial Park then a shuttle on event days.
facts.good_to_know: UCLA football plays home games here in the autumn.

facts.one_liner: ‘The Big House’—the largest stadium in the United States—with its block ‘M’ at midfield.
facts.why_go: Michigan Stadium, home of the University of Michigan Wolverines since 1927, is the largest stadium in the United States and one of the largest in the world, with an official capacity of more than 107,000. The bowl is sunk partly below ground level, so it looks modest from outside until you step in. College football Saturdays in Ann Arbor are an unforgettable American spectacle.
facts.best_time: September–November for home football games; autumn colours in Ann Arbor peak in October.
facts.how_to_get_there: Detroit Metropolitan Airport (DTW) is about 30 minutes’ drive; the stadium is a walk from downtown Ann Arbor.
facts.good_to_know: Big rivalry games (such as Ohio State) sell out early. Bag rules are strict—check before you go.

Home runs over the right-field wall land in McCovey Cove, where kayakers wait to catch them.

facts.how_to_get_there: In SoMa, served by Muni Metro (King St & 2nd St) and a walk from Caltrain’s 4th & King station.

facts.one_liner: A riverside ballpark with downtown Pittsburgh and the yellow Clemente Bridge beyond the outfield.
facts.why_go: PNC Park opened in 2001 on the north shore of the Allegheny River and is often ranked among baseball’s best ballparks for its intimate size and view: over the outfield rise the downtown skyline and the yellow Roberto Clemente Bridge, which closes to traffic on game days so fans can walk across.
facts.best_time: April–September; summer evenings for skyline sunsets.
facts.how_to_get_there: Walk across the Roberto Clemente Bridge from downtown, or take the T light rail to North Side station.
facts.good_to_know: Water taxis run on the rivers on some game days. Stadium tours run in season.

Its retractable roof of eight translucent petals opens like a camera shutter, and a 360-degree ‘halo’ video board rings the bowl. It hosted Super Bowl LIII and is a host venue for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
facts.best_time: August–January for NFL; March–October for MLS; stadium tours year-round.
facts.how_to_get_there: In downtown Atlanta; MARTA trains stop at Vine City and GWCC/Philips Arena–CNN Center stations nearby.
facts.good_to_know: Known for low ‘fan-first’ concession prices. Tours include field-level access.

A vast translucent ETFE canopy covers the stadium and its plaza, and a double-sided oval ‘Infinity Screen’ hangs above the field. facts.best_time: September–January for NFL games; concerts year-round.

facts.good_to_know: Parking is expensive—use rideshare zones or shuttles. Stadium tours are available.

facts.good_to_know: Self-guided and art tours showcase the stadium’s contemporary art collection.

facts.why_go: Arthur Ashe Stadium opened in 1997 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows–Corona Park and is the largest tennis stadium in the world. Named after the trailblazing champion, it gained a retractable roof in 2016. Night sessions at the US Open, under lights with the New York crowd, are legendary.

facts.why_go: Opened in 1922, Centre Court is the main show court of The Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis Club, where the singles finals are played on grass. A retractable roof was added in 2009. Even outside the tournament, the Wimbledon Lawn Tennis Museum and tours let you look over the court.
facts.best_time: Late June–mid-July for The Championships; museum and tours run most of the year.
facts.how_to_get_there: Southfields (District line) is about 15 minutes’ walk; shuttles run from Wimbledon station during the tournament.
facts.good_to_know: Join ‘The Queue’ for same-day tickets—a Wimbledon tradition. Strawberries and cream are mandatory.

facts.why_go: Court Philippe-Chatrier is the main stadium of the French Open at Roland-Garros, on the edge of the Bois de Boulogne. Rebuilt with a retractable roof that opened in 2020, it is where the clay-court Grand Slam finals are played—Rafael Nadal won 14 titles here. Tours of the site and the Tenniseum museum run outside the tournament.
facts.best_time: Late May–early June for the French Open; tours year-round.
facts.how_to_get_there: Porte d’Auteuil (Métro line 10) is a few minutes’ walk.
facts.good_to_know: Tickets go on sale in spring and sell out fast; early-round grounds passes are easier.

facts.how_to_get_there: Free trams run along Flinders Street; Richmond and Jolimont stations are a short walk.

facts.why_go: Twickenham has hosted England rugby internationals since 1910 and today is the largest dedicated rugby union stadium in the world. facts.best_time: February–March for the Six Nations; autumn for international tests.
facts.how_to_get_there: Twickenham station (trains from London Waterloo, about 30 minutes) is a 10-minute walk.
facts.good_to_know: Book museum and stadium tours ahead—they don’t run on match days.

facts.why_go: Hampden Park has been the home of Scottish national football since 1903; in 1937 it drew a European record crowd of nearly 150,000. Today it hosts Scotland internationals, cup finals and concerts, and the Scottish Football Museum inside tells the story of the game.
facts.best_time: Autumn–spring for internationals and cup finals; museum and tours year-round.
facts.how_to_get_there: Mount Florida and King’s Park stations are a short walk; trains from Glasgow Central take about 10 minutes.
facts.good_to_know: The museum includes the oldest national football trophy in the world, the Scottish Cup.
